items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I have no time.
items.explanation: Review (Unit 2): die Zeit is feminine, so keine Zeit.

items.question: You meet a colleague at 7 p.m. What do you say?
items.explanation: Review (Unit 0): Guten Abend is a hello in the evening. Gute Nacht is only a goodbye, late at night or before bed.

items.question: What time is it?
items.explanation: halb drei = halfway to three = 2:30. Think of Russian половина третьего.

items.question: Which one is 9:45?
items.explanation: 9:45 is a quarter before ten: Viertel vor zehn.

items.instruction: Write the time the official way: 18:20.
items.explanation: Official times: hours, then Uhr, then minutes: achtzehn Uhr zwanzig.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: I work eight hours.
items.explanation: die Stunde (plural die Stunden) = an hour, how long something takes. Uhr is only a time on the clock: um acht Uhr.

items.instruction: Fill in the gap: On Saturday I have time.

items.prompt: In the evening I study German.
items.explanation: All three are right. With the time first, the verb still comes second and ich moves behind it: Am Abend lerne ich Deutsch.

items.text: Ich arbeite von Montag bis Freitag.
items.explanation: von ... bis = from ... to. Days are nouns, so they start with a capital letter.

items.audio: Geöffnet: Montag bis Samstag, von acht bis zwanzig Uhr. Am Sonntag geschlossen.
items.question: When is the shop closed?
items.explanation: geschlossen = closed. Most shops in Germany are closed on Sundays.

items.instruction: Describe your usual Monday in 3-4 sentences, with times: when you work or study, and what you do in the evening. Start at least one sentence with the time (Am Abend ...). Claude will check it.
